transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today. As we all know, the set is scheduled for dismantling on Friday after the final stage shoot, and the current draft plan sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor with selected hero props going to production storage. Before I can approve anything, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their department. If anyone has an exception to the draft plan, you need to state the exact corrective requirement so it can be entered into the meeting record. Let's start going through department by department.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan: the antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rented piece. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go to production storage or salvage. The exact corrective requirement is that the jukebox must be removed from the hero-prop storage list and scheduled for return to the rental owner in its original condition, with return logistics confirmed before Friday's dismantling.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan regarding environmental compliance. The production's city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the vendor this morning that the approved vendor's audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft. The exact corrective requirement is that the compliance packet must be updated to replace the general-salvage draft with the approved vendor's audited plan specifying separate wood and metal recycling bins and a certified transfer record, so the 85 percent diversion threshold is properly documented before Mara approves the plan.
